name: Percentage Meaning, Conversions, and Mental Benchmarks
description: Understand percent as “per hundred” and move fluently among percentages, fractions, decimals, and simple percentage-of quantities.
script_scope: Teach percent as parts per hundred, then convert percent to fraction and decimal and convert fractions/decimals back to percent. Include percentages below 1% and above 100%, mixed-number percentages, and comparison of quantities written in different forms. Build mental benchmarks such as 50%=1/2, 25%=1/4, 20%=1/5, 10%=1/10, 5%=1/20 and 1%=1/100. Explain that “of” means multiply and use these benchmarks to evaluate simple percentages mentally before relying on the x/100 rule. Learners should always identify what one whole or 100% represents.

name: Finding the Part, Whole, or Percentage
description: Solve the three basic percentage questions: find a percentage of a quantity, find what percent one quantity is of another, or recover the whole from a known part.
script_scope: Teach the part-whole-percent triangle through equations: part=(percent/100)×whole, percent=(part/whole)×100, whole=part÷(percent/100). Cover missing percentages, missing wholes, percentages of percentages, differences between two percentages of the same number, and unit conversions before comparing quantities such as grams with kilograms or minutes with hours. Include source-style question-mark equations and situations where the final request is a different percentage of the same recovered whole. Learners should check whether a part smaller than the whole gives a percentage below 100 and whether percentages above 100 are reasonable when the part exceeds the reference whole.

name: Percentage Comparisons, Ratios, and “More/Less Than”
description: Translate statements such as “A is 25% more than B” into ratios and correctly reverse the comparison when the reference quantity changes.
script_scope: Teach that percentage comparisons depend on the reference quantity. Convert “A is R% more than B” to A:B=(100+R):100 and “A is R% less than B” to A:B=(100−R):100. Derive the reverse percentages rather than assuming they are equal. Cover relations such as x% of y = y% of x, p% of A=q% of B, ratios expressed as percentages, chained salary or quantity comparisons, and questions asking what percent one transformed quantity is of another. Include exact fraction answers for repeating percentages when useful. Learners should name the base of every “more than” or “less than” statement before calculating.

name: Increase, Decrease, Reverse Percentage, and Successive Change
description: Use percentage multipliers to move forward or backward through increases and decreases, including successive changes and restoration to an original value.
script_scope: Teach multiplier thinking: +R% means multiply by (1+R/100), −R% means multiply by (1−R/100). Use it to find new values and to reverse from a final value to the original. Cover equal percentage increase/decrease giving a net loss, two successive increases, mixed successive increase/decrease, and the percentage needed to restore a reduced or increased value. Explain why +20% followed by −20% does not cancel: the second percentage uses a different base. Include percentage error as error/original×100 and simple multiplier questions such as the factor that represents a 29.7% increase.

name: Price, Consumption, Expenditure, and Revenue
description: Keep expenditure fixed or track revenue when price and quantity change together, using the product relationship price × quantity.
script_scope: Teach expenditure/revenue as price×quantity. Derive the chapter result that after a price increase of R%, consumption must fall by R/(100+R)×100% to keep expenditure fixed, and after a price decrease of R%, consumption may rise by R/(100−R)×100%. Cover same-money buying-power questions, price changes inferred from extra or fewer units bought, simultaneous price and quantity changes and their net effect on expenditure/revenue, and inverse percentage reasoning such as increasing speed to reduce travel time for the same distance. Include cases where expenditure is allowed to change by a stated percentage rather than remain exactly constant.

name: Income, Expenditure, Savings, Tax, and Commission
description: Model percentage-based money flows involving salary, spending, savings, discounts, taxes, commissions, and slab-like payments.
script_scope: Teach income−expenditure=savings and calculate how separate percentage changes in income and expenditure affect savings. Cover sequential spending of a remaining balance, monthly/annual income conversions, commission as a percentage of sales including a fixed amount plus commission above a threshold, simple progressive/slab-style tax reasoning, surcharge on tax, rebate followed by sales tax, and reverse questions where a known investment or deduction is a percentage of salary. Emphasize that percentages taken “of the remaining amount” use a new base, while percentages explicitly stated “of salary” keep the original base.

name: Examinations, Marks, Passing, and Elections
description: Use percentages to solve marks, pass/fail, valid-vote, election-margin, and target-score problems.
script_scope: Cover examination and election patterns from the chapter: convert marks to percentages, combine subjects with different maximum marks, recover maximum marks or pass marks from “failed by” and “passed by” clues, determine the extra marks needed to reach a target percentage, and solve group pass/fail counts. For elections, distinguish enrolled voters, votes cast, valid votes and candidate shares; solve two-candidate margin questions and invalid-vote chains. Include target questions where a student or team must improve a current percentage over the remaining questions/games. Learners should identify the correct denominator at each stage.

name: Weighted Percentages and Group Composition
description: Combine percentages from groups of different sizes and recover subgroup counts when overall and subgroup percentages are given.
script_scope: Teach why percentages from unequal groups cannot be averaged directly. Use actual counts or weighted contributions to combine pass rates, defect rates, tax rates, literacy rates and other subgroup percentages. Cover male/female or skilled/unskilled splits, percentage composition after removing part of one subgroup, two shipments of different sizes, conditional composition such as capable/incapable candidates with different pass rates, and weighted average return/rate questions. Learners should convert each subgroup percentage into a contribution to the whole before combining.

name: Population Growth, Depreciation, and Repeated Annual Change
description: Apply percentage multipliers repeatedly across years to populations, salaries, investments, asset values, and decay.
script_scope: Teach repeated annual growth P(1+R/100)^n and depreciation P(1−R/100)^n, including reversing to a value n years ago. Cover changing annual rates, one year up and another down, finding a constant annual rate from a multi-year multiplier, comparing appreciation with depreciation, and repeated halving/decay patterns. Explain that annual changes compound because each year starts from the previous year’s value. Include source-style population, salary, tree growth and machine-value contexts without requiring compound-interest terminology.

name: Mixtures, Concentration, and Changing Composition
description: Track the amount of a component while solution weight changes through mixing, adding pure material, adding water, evaporation, or replacement.
script_scope: Teach concentration as component amount/total mixture×100. Cover finding component amount in a solution, adding pure component, diluting by adding water, concentrating by evaporation, mixing two solutions of different strengths, removing and replacing part of a solution, repeated replacement, and “fresh versus dry” fruit problems where the non-water solid remains constant. Make the conserved component explicit before forming equations. Keep this within percentage reasoning rather than introducing a separate alligation method.

name: Overlapping Groups: Both, Either, and Neither
description: Use inclusion-exclusion with percentages or counts to solve two-group overlap questions such as subjects, sports, newspapers, or lunch choices.
script_scope: Teach the two-set percentage formula: either A or B = A + B − both. Use it to find both when everyone belongs to at least one group, neither as 100−union, passed-both from failure percentages, totals when the count in neither is known, and “either but not both” as union−both. Include both percentages and actual counts. Learners should see why the overlap is subtracted once: it was counted twice when A and B were added.

name: Percentage Chains, Remaining Quantities, and Effective Rates
description: Handle multi-stage percentage stories where each stage acts on what remains, and work backward from a final remainder when needed.
script_scope: Teach percentage chains as successive multipliers, especially when wording says “of the remaining.” Cover spending/distribution chains, successive rejection or selection stages, effective rejection across multiple quality checks, repeated sell/leave problems, reverse-working from a final remainder, and chains combining a percentage with a fixed amount. Distinguish percentages of the original from percentages of the current remainder. Include capstones where learners must multiply survival factors first and only then convert back to an effective loss or rejection percentage.
